rv.q: From the moment the curtain went up until the play’s poignant end, they held the audience spellbound.
And star casting is justified with quality theater.
That the play works to the extent it does is a testament to the actors.
"A Steady Rain" is an accessible, star-studded snapshot of the consequences of a Midwestern malaise — commercially packaged, for sure, but still recognizable to any Chicagoan with their eyes open.

And while both men, particularly Craig, acquit themselves well, they can't turn the 90-minute evening into anything more than a chance to see two big-time movie stars emoting up close in a pulpy, plot-heavy entertainment.
Nobody goes to “A Steady Rain,” which ends its hot-ticket limited run on Dec. 6, to look at scenery.
In fact, the acting is so refined that one would love to see the play without such auspicious screen idols, the way it was cast in the original Chicago production.
You may be grabbing tickets for "A Steady Rain" simply to bask in the movie-starry presence of Daniel ("007") Craig and Hugh ("Wolverine") Jackman on Broadway.

cn.t: Craig and Jackman's star power elevates mediocre material in this dark Chicago cop drama. Critics praise both actors' compelling performances, but find Huff's melodramatic two-hander increasingly ridiculous and plot-heavy.

vs.sum: The Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, although some side seats may have partial views. The sound quality is generally strong, enhancing the theatrical experience. However, the seating is tight, which can affect comfort, particularly for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is charming with its historic character, and while facilities are adequate, expect some lines at the bar and restrooms.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Infrared devices available.
